title: One Character Difference
statement:
Decide whether a list contains two words that differ in exactly one position.

Contract
- `words` is non-null. Every entry is non-null, has the same length, and contains lowercase letters. The list may be empty.
- Return true if there are two distinct entries with equal length that differ at exactly one character index and match at every other index.
- Equal duplicate words do not count because they differ in zero positions.
- Do not mutate the array or its strings.

Examples
- `hasOneCharacterDifference(new String[]{"abcd", "acbd", "aacd"})` returns `true` because `abcd` and `aacd` differ only at index 1.
- `hasOneCharacterDifference(new String[]{"ab", "cd", "yz"})` returns `false`.
- `hasOneCharacterDifference(new String[]{"same", "same"})` returns `false`.
hints: A brute force comparison of every pair is simple but repeats most character checks.
For each word, hide one position with a marker. Two words with the same masked form differ in at most that one position.
Store masked forms in a set and make sure the matching words are not identical. Intended complexity: O(n) time and O(n) extra space when word length is treated as part of each processed item.
inputSyntax: Input: equal-length lowercase words separated by commas, for example: abcd,acbd,aacd
